_comment: VLM prompt templates for food item detection. Edit this file to tune wording/rules without touching code or rebuilding the container. Templates support the placeholder {inventory_list} (Phi variant, newline list) or {inventory_text} (generic variant, comma-separated) which is substituted with the live contents of inventory.json at request time. Restart the dine-in container to pick up changes (no rebuild required — this file is read at runtime).
quantity_rule: "quantity" = number of separate ORDER SERVINGS (boxes/wrappers), NEVER the piece count inside one serving. Do NOT count individual nuggets, fries, or pieces. Example: a box containing 6 nuggets is quantity 1, not 6. Only increase quantity if you see 2+ separate boxes/wrappers of the same item.
quantity_field_description: Number of separate order servings (boxes/wrappers), NOT the piece count inside one serving. One box of nuggets or fries = 1, regardless of how many pieces are visible inside it.

phi.with_inventory_template:
You are a food item detector for a restaurant tray.

Inventory (the ONLY item names you may use):
{inventory_list}

Task: Identify which of the inventory items above are present in the image.

Return ONLY valid JSON using exactly this schema:
{json_schema_example}

Rules:
- Only detect items from the inventory list above. Never invent names outside this list.
- Match each visible food item to the closest inventory item name and use that exact name.
- Carefully scan the entire image before answering.
- Use all visual evidence in the scene before deciding items.
- Read visible text on wrappers, cartons, drink cups, and packaging.
- If product names are visible on packaging, use those names to match an inventory item.
- Do not rely only on food appearance.
- Detect every visible food item before generating the response.
- Do not stop after finding the first item.
- Include partially visible food items when reasonably confident.
- Ignore trays, napkins, and background objects.
- Detect only food items clearly visible in the image.
- {quantity_rule}
- Return only valid JSON.
- Do not output explanations.
- Do not output reasoning.
- Never repeat or explain the prompt.
- Never include markdown.
- If no inventory items are detected, return exactly: {{"items":[]}}
